scene_text: Sati, surrounded by shocked sages and blazing ritual fires, leaps into the sacrificial flames after denouncing her father Daksha.
Rama revealing his blazing Vishvarupa to Sati, with countless gods, suns, and cosmic beings appearing within his radiant universal body.
Shiva tearing a braid from his matted hair and hurling it to the mountain, from which the colossal warrior Virabhadra and fierce Bhadra Kali emerge.
Shiva tears a braid from his matted hair and hurls it onto a mountain, from which the fierce thousand‑armed warrior Virabhadra erupts.
Sati seated in deep yogic meditation before the sacrificial fire, then leaping into the rising flames while sages and gods watch in shock.
Rama reveals his universal form to Sati, his body containing suns, gods, and countless beings shining in cosmic radiance.
Cosmic Tripura battle: Shiva rides a celestial chariot made of Earth with Sun and Moon as wheels, Meru as the bow and Vishnu as the arrow aimed at the three shining demon cities.
The newborn Skanda appears at dawn—six‑headed and twelve‑armed, shining like the sun—while gods shower flowers from the sky and Vedic chants resound.
The radiant six‑headed infant Skanda appears at dawn amid Vedic chants while gods shower flowers from the sky.
From the palace terrace Parvati gazes down at the arriving wedding procession as Shiva looks up, their eyes meeting in a silent exchange of divine love.
Shiva stands before the fallen body of the clay-born guardian while Parvati weeps, as attendants bring the severed elephant head of Gajasura to restore the child to life.
Siva rides a cosmic chariot made of Earth with sun and moon as wheels and fires a divine arrow that destroys the three floating cities of Tripura.
Goddess Durga leaps onto the buffalo-demon Mahishasura, pinning him under her foot and thrusting a spear into his body as the gods watch.
In the wedding hall Shiva ties the mangala sutra around Parvati’s neck as priests chant Vedic hymns and gods shower blessings.
A golden screen falls away at the auspicious moment as Shiva and Parvati gaze into each other's eyes during their wedding ceremony.
Shiva and Parvati arrive at glittering Mount Kailasa while gods, celestial beings, animals, and the radiant silver mountain itself seem to welcome the newlywed divine couple.
Siva attaches the elephant head of Gajasura onto the lifeless body of Ganapati as Parvati watches in grief and hope.
Parvati steps into a blazing sacrificial fire during her penance, yet the flames turn cool around her as the disguised Shiva watches in astonishment.
The Shiva linga cracks open with a cosmic roar as three-eyed Shiva emerges brandishing a trident and confronting the god of death.
Princess Srimati passes by Narada in the royal court and garlands the disguised Prince Vishnu while the sage sits proudly, unaware of the monkey face he bears.
Shiva opens his blazing third eye and a burst of fire reduces Manmatha to ashes in the flowering Bilva garden.
Shiva dismounts his bull before a temple shrine where Rama and Sita appear alive to bless the bashful bridegroom while celestial guests watch in awe.
Siva hurls his spear and Ganapati’s head is severed while the boy stands guarding Parvati’s bath door with a staff.
Shiva reveals his true radiant form before Parvati after her passionate defense of him, the forest hermitage glowing with divine light.
Siva briefly reveals multiple divine forms—Vishnu with four arms and then Nataraja dancing—before vanishing before the astonished crowd.
Young Markandeya clings tightly to a Shiva linga while Yama on his buffalo casts a glowing noose that encircles both the boy and the idol.
Shiva and Shakti gaze at each other in radiant stillness as a sapphire-blue four‑armed child, Vishnu, manifests before them in a burst of light.
Shiva arrives on his white bull Nandi while gods, sages, and celestial beings fill the Himalayan capital in celebration.
The gods stand outside Shiva’s guarded chamber chanting 'Namah Sivaya' in devotion as Nandi keeps watch at the doorway of the divine couple.
Arjuna battles a radiant tribal hunter—Shiva in disguise—in a forest, arrows flying as the god’s wild retinue surrounds them.
Parvati steps into a blazing fire during her vow, yet the flames cool harmlessly around her body.
Narada stares into a mirror in shock as he sees a monkey’s face attached to Vishnu’s divine body after the failed svayamvara.
Menaka kisses Parvati farewell as the bride sits in a golden palanquin departing for Kailasa while mountains, animals, and flowers seem to mourn.
Ganapati sits on darbha grass chanting 'Namah Sivaaya' while reverently circling Shiva and Parvati twenty‑one times as divine light surrounds the family.
An endless pillar of blazing light appears between Brahma flying upward as a swan and Vishnu diving downward to find its base.
In the palace courtyard, the disguised wandering monk dances and blows a conch while Parvati recognizes him as Shiva and bows amid astonished onlookers.
Parvati stands unmoving amid five blazing fires during her severe penance in the forest while her maids watch from afar.
The magnificent horses in the royal stables transform overnight into howling jackals that scatter through the dark streets of Madura.
A young Upamanyu meditates under a banyan tree as a tiger roars nearby and Shiva and Parvati appear before the fearless child.
Nandanar stands before the shrine of Nataraja as a sacred flame suddenly flares up and engulfs him in radiant light.
Siva and Parvati dance joyfully among peacocks in a secluded arbor on Mount Kailasa.
In the wedding hall, Shiva and Sati sit on a golden plank garlanding each other while gods shower flower petals from the sky.
Chitrarekha magically lifts the sleeping Aniruddha together with his bed from Dvaraka and carries him through the night sky.
Lord Siva’s ghostly attendants ride into Madura on dazzling horses as dust rises over the city and the imprisoned minister watches in awe.
Under a vast banyan tree on Mount Kailasa, ash-covered Shiva sits in deep meditation while sages and celestial beings gather around him.
